title: Caleb Durbin’s resurgence has been a symbol of Red Sox’ improbable run
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Caleb Durbin hit his first career grand slam in the Red Sox's 14-2 win over the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday.
The Boston Red Sox have won 24 of their last 27 games, leading the American League in home runs during this stretch.
Since mid-May, Durbin has improved significantly, batting .308 with 10 home runs, transforming into a key player for Boston.

title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (Aug. 5)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: Abington's priciest sale: One-family Colonial at 22 Nardone Circle sold for $1,185,000 on a 45,284-square-foot lot.
In Arlington, 85 Oakland Ave. Colonial sold for $2,755,000, featuring 2,498 square feet with 4 bedrooms and 3 baths.
Belmont saw a sale at 100 Village Hill Road, a one-family garrison, for $2,225,000 on a 15,842-square-foot lot.

title: Jarren Duran: ‘I thought I was going to be released’ by Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran expressed surprise at not being released by the Red Sox amid recent trades and roster changes.
Duran admitted to struggling offensively this season, maintaining a .200 batting average and a .257 on-base percentage.
Despite trade rumors, the Red Sox kept Duran, who hopes to contribute to a potential playoff push.

title: Wu, Councilor Louijeune lead more than 100 elected officials in urging Congress to extend protections for Haitians
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu and Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune lead officials urging Congress to extend TPS for Haitians until 2029.
104 local officials sent a letter to the U.S. Senate following the Supreme Court's ruling allowing TPS termination for Haitians.
Haitian TPS holders contribute an estimated $4.4 to $5.9 billion annually to the U.S. economy, says the officials' letter.

title: Durbin hits grand slam and Abreu goes deep twice as streaking Red Sox rout White Sox 14-2
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Caleb Durbin's grand slam and Wilyer Abreu's two homers helped the Red Sox rout the White Sox 14-2.
Patrick Sandoval earned his first win since 2024, striking out five and allowing two runs in over five innings.
Brayan Bello secured his first career save as the Red Sox extended their winning streak to six games.

title: What Adley Rutschman said about joining Red Sox after blockbuster trade
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman joins the Red Sox in a trade involving Carlos Narvaez and three prospects.
Rutschman is recovering from wrist inflammation and currently progressing in a hitting rehabilitation.
Interim manager Chad Tracy sees Rutschman as a key addition to improve Red Sox's catching and offense.

title: Lawsuit against Suffolk DA, BPD aims to force release of footage of fatal police shooting in Roxbury
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Lawyers for Civil Rights filed a lawsuit against Suffolk DA and BPD for withholding footage of Stephenson King's fatal shooting.
Footage requests under public records law were denied, citing investigatory concerns and potential impact on jurors and witnesses.
Boston officer Nicholas O'Malley, charged with manslaughter, fatally shot King during a carjacking response in March.

title: Could Roman Anthony, Garrett Crochet return to Red Sox this season?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Roman Anthony resumed batting practice after recovering from a wrist sprain and ligament injury, aiming for a September return.
Garrett Crochet began throwing after shoulder inflammation and lat strain, but faces a challenging timeline to return this season.
Manager Chad Tracy provided updates on several injured players, including Trevor Story, who is nearing a rehab assignment.

title: ‘We’ve got to make up for lost time’: After lengthy absence, Gabe Jacas faces a new challenge
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Gabe Jacas signs a 4-year deal with the Patriots, worth up to $8.6 million, after lengthy negotiations.
Jacas missed months of practice due to injury concerns and contract issues but has now joined training camp.
Coach Mike Vrabel emphasizes Jacas needs to catch up but is pleased with his eagerness and progress so far.

title: Skeletal remains found in South Boston home turn out to be animal bones, police say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Boston Police discovered animal bones at 8 Glover Court, South Boston, initially believed to be human remains.
The remains were found with shoes in a bag; police responded to the scene on Monday afternoon.
The Massachusetts state medical examiner confirmed the bones were not human, investigation remains ongoing.
